turns.user: My brakes have been squealing for a few weeks
turns.text:
Your brakes are on-time per your last service ~2 months ago. But squealing for weeks deserves a look — could be pad wear indicators (designed to squeal as a heads-up), or something else. 

Quick question: does the squeal happen mostly when you first hit the brakes, or does it stick around through the whole stop?

turns.user: Mostly when I first hit the brakes, then it goes quiet
turns.text:
That's the classic wear-indicator pattern — pad sensors trigger on first braking to alert you when they're getting thin. Your brakes are on_time per your last service ~2 months ago, but squealing that specific way is worth a closer look.

Here's the thing: brakes look fine on the record, but squealing through only the first contact is the signature move of pads nearing end-of-life, even if the last service was recent. A diagnostic would be the safe play to confirm. That said — do you want a Diagnostic Scan to have a mechanic pin down exactly what's going on, or would you rather just book a Brake Pad Replacement straight up based on the pattern?

(Separately: I'm also flagging a temperature / overheating warning light in your car's known issues. Have you seen that one, or is that new to you?)

Two unblock paths: (A) decouple the counter from skipPersist (a chat.ts-only change, out of scope for the QA-lead adaptation dispatch), or (B) ship a harness-side seed mutation that sets diagnostic_turn_count=5 before the final turn (also touches convex/). Re-enable once either lands. Intent preserved verbatim — do not delete.
